claims.text: As-received Q235 steel has a heterogeneous microstructure with variable grain sizes and inclusions.
Annealing Q235 steel at 550 °C for 2 hours in air will refine its grain structure.
Annealing Q235 steel at 550 °C for 2 hours in air will homogenize or redistribute its inclusions.
The annealing treatment will increase the proportion of low-angle grain boundaries.
A refined grain structure and more uniform inclusion distribution will promote formation and adhesion of a continuous protective oxide/hydroxide film.
Microstructural heterogeneities in Q235 steel act as localized anodic sites and pit-initiation triggers.
The annealing treatment will reduce microstructural heterogeneities that act as corrosion-initiation sites.
The annealing-induced microstructure will enhance development of a predominantly iron oxide/hydroxide passive layer.
The protective layer will impede aggressive ions such as chloride and slow diffusion-driven corrosion.
The annealing treatment will suppress corrosion initiation and propagation during room-temperature exposure to 3.5 wt% H2SO4 relative to untreated Q235 steel.
The annealing treatment will suppress degradation during 900 °C cyclic exposure to 75% Na2SO4/25% NaCl relative to untreated Q235 steel.
Annealed specimens will have greater Vickers microhardness than untreated specimens.
Annealed specimens will exhibit lower corrosion current than untreated specimens.
Annealed specimens will exhibit greater polarization resistance than untreated specimens.
Annealed specimens will exhibit reduced mass gain during cyclic hot-corrosion exposure compared with untreated specimens.
The predicted improvement is limited to approximately 550 °C for 2 hours and the specified exposure environments, and may change with treatment time, temperature, or salt composition.
Analogous material systems indicate that grain refinement can promote passive-film formation and retard corrosion.
The quantitative interplay among microstructure, inclusions, and passive-film chemistry in Q235 steel remains unresolved.
